items.title: TN cop clings to SUV roof for 30 km to stop gutka smugglers in Coimbatore
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. For nearly 30 km, a head constable clung to the roof rails of a speeding SUV as police chased its occupants, who were allegedly trying to flee with around 170 kg of gutka and other banned tobacco products in Coimbatore on Sunday, September 27. The chase ended near Thekkalur on the Tiruppur district border, where police arrested three men and seized the contraband. The incident began around 5.45 am when a team from Kovilpalayam police station, led by Sub Inspector V Vignesh and Head Constable M Velmurugan, was checking vehicles between Vilankurichi and Kalappati. The officers attempted to stop a Karnataka-registered SUV suspected to be carrying gutka. According to the police, the occupants initially refused to stop but slowed down later. When the officers noticed bundles inside the vehicle, Vignesh attempted to search it. The occupants allegedly pushed the policemen, shut the doors, and accelerated towards Avinashi. Velmurugan reportedly told The New Indian Express that the driver suddenly accelerated while the police were trying to stop the vehicle, trapping his hand in the door. It was argued that the mandatory requirement of the voter ID card of Punjab State for getting the scheme benefits clearly indicates that its object is only to secure votes from the beneficiaries. While adjourning the matter to October 5, the Court said, "Learned Additional Advocate General, Punjab opposes the petitioner’s claim and seeks adjournment in order to obtain instructions and clarify the purpose for which Voter ID card is made mandatory for grant of benefit under the Scheme."
